title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named CSUSM spaces for studying, making, meeting, recharging, recreation, and campus events, each tied to a direct university source.

cards.title: Make Something Between Classes
cards.subtitle: A hands-on makerspace inside Kellogg Library
cards.notes: Stop on the library’s second floor to try a short craft, play a game, or explore the shared tools and materials available here.
cards.short_summary: A library makerspace built for experimenting, creating, and learning alongside other campus community members.
cards.evidence_claim: The Makery is a second-floor University Library makerspace where the CSUSM community can gather, create, socialize, explore, and learn skills with tools and materials.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of Kellogg Library; consult the page’s current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Put a Group Session on the Calendar
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms across three library floors
cards.notes: Reserve ahead, bring at least one study partner, and use the whiteboard and power outlets to turn a meeting into a working session.
cards.short_summary: Forty-two reservable rooms give CSUSM student groups an enclosed place to work together.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library has 42 group study rooms on floors two, four, and five, equipped with tables, chairs, whiteboards, and power outlets for current CSUSM student groups.
cards.access_notes: Current CSUSM students must reserve rooms in advance; group rooms require at least two students.

cards.title: Move an Idea Off the Page
cards.subtitle: A project space in the Extended Learning Building
cards.notes: Use the movable workspace for collaborative planning, then look for a class or public event that puts the video wall or makerspace into use.
cards.short_summary: A flexible project and event space designed to connect ideas with collaborative, hands-on work.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2,800-square-foot Innovation Hub occupies the Extended Learning Building’s ground floor and includes movable furniture, a video wall, and a makerspace for classes and public events.
cards.source_title: Bright Ideas: Under Neufeldt, Spirit of Innovation Is Shining at CSUSM
cards.access_notes: Located on the ground floor of the Extended Learning Building; access may depend on scheduled classes or events.

cards.title: Reset at Street Level
cards.subtitle: The first-floor base for time between classes
cards.notes: Bring food to reheat, charge up near the computers, or use the lockers and printing station before heading back across campus.
cards.short_summary: A practical first-floor lounge combining seats with commuter-focused everyday facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The current USU floor plan identifies a first-floor Commuter Lounge with microwaves, computers, PAW Printing, lockers, a smart TV, and a nearby restroom and shower.
cards.access_notes: Located on floor one of the University Student Union, reached from the street-level entrance.

cards.title: Turn a Break Into Game Time
cards.subtitle: Games and lounging on the USU’s fourth floor
cards.notes: Meet friends here for a casual game or a lounge break, and check on-site details before choosing any activity that carries a fee.
cards.short_summary: A named fourth-floor social space where students can play games and spend time between commitments.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM’s Student Life playbook describes the USU Activity Center as a space for students to play games, lounge, and purchase discounted tickets.
cards.access_notes: Located in the University Student Union; individual games or ticket offerings may require payment.

cards.title: Take the Conversation Upstairs
cards.subtitle: An outdoor fourth-floor patio beside the green roof
cards.notes: Carry a conversation or reading break outdoors, use the patio seating, and leave planted green-roof areas undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: An elevated outdoor gathering area that adds fresh-air seating to the student union.
cards.evidence_claim: The current University Student Union floor plan names the Rooftop Patio on floor four alongside the building’s green roof and dining areas.
cards.access_notes: Located on floor four of the University Student Union; availability can be affected by reserved events.

cards.title: Find the Outdoor Stage
cards.subtitle: A campus event space built into the student union
cards.notes: Check the campus event listings, then use the amphitheater as a clear meetup point before a performance, fair, or program begins.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable open-air venue where student programming can spill into the center of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Student Union includes an open-air amphitheater, and its sliding stage doors can connect it with the ballroom for combined events.
cards.source_title: The New Heart of CSUSM, USU Opens Its Doors
cards.access_notes: Event setup or reservations may limit access; check the event listing associated with a planned visit.

cards.title: Start With the Organization Fair
cards.subtitle: A plaza used for student-group introductions
cards.notes: Use a scheduled organization fair to compare clubs in one stop, ask direct questions, and note follow-up meetings that fit your interests.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus plaza documented as a gathering point for student-organization outreach.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM listed Forum Plaza as one of the locations for its January 29, 2026 Student Organization Fair, where students could learn about campus organizations and clubs.
cards.access_notes: The cited fair occurred January 29, 2026; consult current campus events for the plaza’s next scheduled program.

cards.title: Look Beyond the Main Gym Door
cards.subtitle: Recreation and meeting space beside the Sports Center
cards.notes: Check Campus Recreation requirements before arriving, then choose between the fitness center, gymnasium, or a scheduled campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding recreation facility combining exercise areas, meeting rooms, and campus recreation offices.
cards.evidence_claim: The M. Gordon Clarke Field House contains a fitness center, gymnasium, locker rooms, conference rooms, and offices for Campus Recreation and Cougar Athletics.
cards.source_title: Icons of CSUSM: The Stories Behind Building Names
cards.access_notes: Facility use can be membership-, program-, or schedule-dependent; verify current Campus Recreation requirements.

cards.title: Take Study Notes to the Terrace
cards.subtitle: An outdoor work spot attached to Markstein Hall
cards.notes: Bring material suited to a short outdoor session, use the terrace between classes, and move inside if weather or an event changes the setup.
cards.short_summary: A named terrace that extends Markstein Hall’s academic environment into an outdoor study setting.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM’s official walking-tour brochure states that Markstein Hall includes a terrace described as another place to study.
cards.access_notes: The terrace is associated with Markstein Hall; building operations or reserved activities may affect access.
